items.title: European stocks slip as Iran conflict enters sixth day

featured_image.name: European markets move sharply lower as global turmoil deepens

items.description:
European equities fell on Thursday as a brief market rebound faded and the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its sixth day, renewing fears over energy supply disruptions and the broader economic fallout of the conflict.

The STOXX 50 dropped 0.6% and the STOXX 600 slipped 0.3% in early trading, erasing gains from Wednesday's relief rally. The pullback came as investors reassessed the likelihood of a prolonged conflict following Iran's claims of control over the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint that carries roughly one-fifth of the world's total oil consumption.[1][2][3]

items.title: Bulk carrier signals 'China owner' to cross Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: The Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description:
A bulk carrier signaled it was Chinese-owned as it transited the Strait of Hormuz early Thursday, underscoring how commercial vessels are improvising to ensure safe passage through the critical waterway as the war between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition enters its second week.

The Iron Maiden changed its destination signal from "For Orders" to "CHINA OWNER" as it pushed through the passage while hugging the Omani coastline, according to ship-tracking data reported by Bloomberg and analytics firm Kpler. The vessel, which had been in the Persian Gulf since December delivering multiple shipments, is operated by Cetus Maritime Shanghai. A spokesperson for the company declined to comment, citing crew safety concerns.[1][2]

items.title: Sri Lanka recovers 87 bodies from Iranian warship sunk by US submarine

featured_image.name: Sri Lanka recovers 87 bodies from Iranian warship sunk off its coast by a US submarine

items.description:
A U.S. Navy fast-attack submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on Tuesday with a single Mk-48 torpedo, marking the first time an American submarine has destroyed an enemy warship since 1945, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed at a Pentagon briefing Wednesday. Sri Lankan authorities said they recovered 87 bodies and rescued 32 survivors from the 180-member crew, with roughly 60 sailors still unaccounted for as search operations continued Thursday.[1][2]

"Yesterday, in the Indian Ocean, an American submarine sunk an Iranian warship that thought it was safe in international waters," Hegseth told reporters. "Instead, it was sunk by a torpedo. Quiet death".[3]

items.title: Jet fuel hits record as Iran war chokes global supply

featured_image.name: Jet fuel prices up as demand jumps, refinery outages limit supply | Reuters

items.description:
Jet fuel prices in Singapore rocketed 72% to a record $225.44 a barrel on Wednesday, according to Reuters, underscoring how the war in Iran is rapidly translating into economic pain for energy consumers across Asia and beyond. The spot price of jet kerosene has now climbed 140% since February 27, the day before the United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran in what has been dubbed "Operation Epic Fury".[1][2]

The surge in aviation fuel — outpacing even the sharp rally in crude oil — reflects mounting fears about a prolonged disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption flows. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has declared "complete control" over the strait and warned that any vessel attempting to pass would be targeted.[3][4][1]

items.title: Alibaba forms AI task force after Qwen chief's abrupt exit

featured_image.name: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu takes over as e-commerce head as growth ...

items.description:
Alibaba is setting up a new internal task force to accelerate its AI model development, a day after the abrupt resignation of Qwen technical lead Lin Junyang rattled investors and the open-source AI community.

CEO Eddie Wu will coordinate the task force alongside Alibaba Cloud CTO Zhou Jingren and Group CTO Wu Zeming, the company said Thursday in a staff letter that also confirmed Lin's departure and pledged to channel additional resources toward AI development. "In technology, standing still means falling behind," Wu wrote. "Advancing foundation models is a core strategic priority for our future."[1][2]

items.title: Russian oil tankers reroute to India as Hormuz crisis chokes supply

featured_image.name: Russian Oil Cargoes Swing Back to India as Iran War Hits ...

items.description:
Two Russian oil tankers carrying a combined 1.4 million barrels of Urals crude have switched their destinations from East Asia to India, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa, as the escalating Middle East conflict forces New Delhi to revisit the Russian barrels it had been shunning under American pressure.[1]

The Odune, a Suezmax carrying 730,000 barrels, arrived at the eastern port of Paradip on Wednesday, while the Matari, an Aframax with more than 700,000 barrels, is expected to reach Vadinar in western India on Thursday, Bloomberg reported. A third vessel, the Indri, made a sharp northward turn in the Arabian Sea this week toward India with another 730,000 barrels of Urals aboard. All three tankers were sanctioned by the United Kingdom and the European Union this year.[1]
